newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Dlr/yen vol up as spot extends above 118.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Dlr/yen vol up as spot extends above 118.

text.p: Dollar/yen option volatilities ticked higher as the spot rate extended recent gains above 118 and the psychologicial 120 level loomed.
Dealers said demand for near-term dollar call strikes up to 120 yen continued and noted the ongoing demand for longer-term -- out to one year -- dollar calls at the 125 strike.

"The market perception is that the Japanese recovery is stalling and it looks less likely we'll see higher rates there any time soon," said a U.S. bank options dealer. "People are looking for more dollar upside and the risk reversal has gone deeper for yen puts."

The weaker economic outlook for Japan was highlighted in this morning's June preliminary industrial output data which registered a 3.1 percent monthly fall. Although broadly in line with expectations, it put further into the background concerns of a Japanese interest rate hike in the near future.

However, dealers were mindful of strong technical resistance at 119 yen, a 50 percent retracement of dollar/yen's May to June decline, as well as the perception the 120 yen level is the upper boundary of Japanese authorities' tolerance range.
"Vols are likely to be quite sensitive to spot moves as we get up to 120, the risk of a pullback from those levels is that much greater," said a UK bank dealer.
One-month dollar/yen vol was trading at 11.6/11.8 percent compared with 10.7/11.2 percent late Tuesday. One-year vol was also higher at 12.0/12.2 percent from 11.5/11.7.
